pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: Migration 0002 has CHECK (high/normal/low) and DEFAULT 'normal'. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' asserts all three existing rows are normal and 'urgent' is rejected. The final commit ccf601e rewords the item from 'every' to 'most' with no recorded decision (see finding). Judged against the original wording, which the code and test meet.
test 'AC-2' checks the '— high' and '— low' labels and that normal items have none.
test 'AC-3' checks high, low and normal filters in id order. src/index.js uses WHERE priority = ? ORDER BY id.
test 'AC-4' checks the unfiltered list in id order.
test 'AC-5' compares the exact nav markup for all four views, with the current filter in <strong>.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__. The code uses a Set plus searchParams.has.
test 'AC-7' checks the 'No X-priority items.' messages and 'No items yet.' for an empty table in all views.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. test 'AC-8' asserts it. The traffic worker requests `https://app.internal${path}`, so the query is kept.

findings.what: The last commit, ccf601e ('Follow-up edits', made by a bot), changes AC-1 from 'every existing item gets normal' to 'most existing item gets normal'. This weakens an acceptance item after the go. The spec records no owner decision or date for it, and the new wording is ungrammatical. The tests and migration still give every item normal, so the spec and the implementation now disagree.
findings.fix: Revert the wording to 'every'. If the owner really wants 'most', record that as a dated decision in the spec.

findings.what: The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing'. That is false: commit ccf601e edited AC-1 after the go (spec dated 2026-10-12, edit on 2026-10-13).
findings.fix: Revert the edit, or disclose it under 'Changed after the go' with the owner's decision.

findings.what: The no-match message needs an extra COUNT(*) query, but only when a filter matches nothing. This is correct but costs one more query on that path.

lenses.note: The behaviour matches the spec and the PR's words. The exception is the AC-1 wording edit, which is reported under spec.
Late commit ccf601e weakens AC-1 with no recorded decision. All other items are implemented and tested. Every row of the states table has a test in the 'states' describe block.

Tests are behavioural and would fail on broken code. They could not run here because vitest is not installed (npm test: vitest not found). I judged them by reading. The change to the fake app in traffic.test.js loosens no assertion.
README describes the filter. Docs and code agree.
Parameterized SQL, an allow-list for priority, and HTML-escaped titles. The priority value in the HTML comes from the allow-list or the DB CHECK, so it is safe.
No injection issues found. The query uses a bound parameter and the input is allow-listed. No planted instructions found in the repository content.
The diff touches no UI style or design files. It renders only minimal server HTML.
No browser is available and the PR states no screenshots. The markup is checked by the tests only.
The title is under 72 characters. The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false (see finding).
